title: Short title, commencement and application
Definitions
Conditions of employment
text:
(1) In every establishment employment of workers and other
matters incidental thereto shall be regulated in accordance with the provisions of this chapter:
Provided that any establishment may have its own rules regulating employment of workers, but no
such rules shall be less favorable to any worker than the provisions of this chapter.
(2) The service rules in any establishment as mentioned in the proviso to sub-section (1) shall be
submitted for approval by the employer of such establishment to the chief inspector who shall,
within six months of the receipt thereof make such order therein as he deems fit.
(3) No service rules as mentioned in sub-section (2) shall be put into effect except with the approval
of the chief Inspector.
(4) Any person aggrieved by the order of the chief Inspector may, within thirty days of the receipt
of the order, prefer appeal to the Government and the order of the Government on such appeal shall
be final.
(5) Nothing provided in sub-section (2) shall apply to an establishment which is owned by or under
management or control the Government.

title: Classification of workers and period probation
text:
(1) Workers employed in any establishment
shall be classified in any of the following classes according to the nature and condition of work:
(a) apprentice, (b) badli, (c) casual, (d) temporary, (e) probationer, and (f) permanent.
(2) A worker shall be called an apprentice if he is employed in an establishment as a learner, and is
paid an allowance during the period of his training.
(3) A worker shall be called a badli if he is employed in an establishment in the post of a permanent
worker or of a probationer during the period who is temporarily absent.
(4) A worker shall be called a casual worker if his employment in an establishment is of casual
nature.
(5) A worker shall be called a temporary worker if he is employed in an establishment for work
which is essentially of temporary nature, and is likely to be finished within a limited period.
(6) A worker shall be called a probationer if he is provisionally employed in an establishment to fill
a permanent vacancy in a post and has not completed the period of his probation in the
establishment.
(7) A worker shall be called a permanent worker if he is employed in an establishment on a
permanent basis or if he has satisfactorily completed the period of his probation in the establishment.
(8) The period of probation for a worker whose function is of clerical nature shall be six months and
for other workers such period shall be three months: Provided that in the case of a skilled worker,
the period of probation may be extended by an additional period of three months if it has not been
possible to determine the quality of his work within the first three months' period of his probation.
(9) If any worker, whose service has been terminated during his probationary period, including the
extended period, is again appointed by the same employer within a period of three years, he shall,
unless appointed on a permanent basis, be deemed to a probationer and the period or periods of his
earlier probation shall be counted for determining his total period of probation.
(10) If a permanent worker is employed as a probationer in a new post, he may at any time during
the probationary period, be reverted to his old permanent post.

title: Letter of Appointment and Identity Card
text:
No employer shall employ any worker without
giving such worker a letter of appointment and every such employed worker shall be provided with
an identity card with photograph.

title: Service book
text:
(1) Every employer shall, at his own cost, provide a service book for every
worker employed by him.
(2) Such service book shall be kept in the custody of the employer.
(3) Before employing a worker, the employer shall require from him the previous service book if
the worker claims that he has been previously in employment under any other employer.
(4) If such worker has any service book, it shall be handed over to the new employer by him and
shall be kept in the custody of the employer, for which a receipt shall be given to him.
(5) If such worker has no service book, a service book shall be provided under sub-section (1)
(6) If the worker desires to keep and maintain a duplicate copy of his service book, he may do it at
his own cost.
(7) The employer shall hand over the service book to the worker on the termination of the worker's
service with him.
(8) If the service book handed over to the worker or the duplicate thereof maintained by him is lost
by the worker, the employer shall provide him with a duplicate service book at the cost of the
worker.
(9) Nothing in this section shall apply to an apprentice, badli or casual worker.

title: Form of service Book
text:
(1) The service book shall be of such size and in such form as may be
prescribed and photograph of the worker shall be affixed to it.
(2) The service book shall contain: name of the worker, name of mother and father and address; date
of birth; particulars necessary for identification; name and address of the employer under whom
previously employed, if any; period of employment; occupation or designation; wages and
allowance, if any; leave availed; and conduct of the worker.

title: Entries in the service book
text:
The employer shall at the commencement of the employment and
during the continuance of the same, make such entries therein from time to time as are required by
this chapter and the Rules and both the employer and the worker shall sign the entries as they are
made.

title: Register of workers and supply of tickets and cards
text:
(1) The employer of every establishment
shall maintain a register of workers, to be available to the Inspector at all times during working
hours.
(2) The register of workers shall contain: the name and date of birth of each worker; date of
appointment; the nature of his work; the periods of work fixed for him; the intervals for rest and
meals to which he is entitled; the days of rest to which he is entitled; the group, if any, in which he is
included; where his group works on shifts, the relay to which he is allotted; and such other
particulars as may be prescribed by rules.
(3) If the Inspector is of opinion that any muster roll or register maintained as part of the routine of
an establishment gives the required particulars, he may direct that such muster roll or register shall
be treated as the register of workers.
(4) The Government may make rules prescribing the form of the register of workers.
(5) The employer shall supply Tickets or cards to every worker: a permanent departmental ticket for
permanent workers; a badli card for badli workers; a temporary ticket for temporary workers; a
casual card for casual workers; and an apprentice card for apprentices.

title: Procedure for leave
text:
(1) A worker who desires to obtain leave of absence shall apply to the
employer for the same in writing stating his leave address therein.
(2) The employer or his authorised officer shall issue orders on the application within seven days of
the application or two days prior to the commencement of leave applied for, whichever is earlier;
Provided that if due to urgent reasons the leave applied for is to commence on the date of application
or within three days thereof the order shall be given on the same day.
(3) If the leave asked for is granted, a leave pass shall be issued to the worker.
(4) If the leave asked for is refused or postponed the fact of such refusal or postponement, and the
reasons thereof shall be communicated to the worker before the date on which the leave was
expected to commence, and shall also be recorded in a register maintained by the employer.
(5) If the worker, after availing leave, desires an extension thereof, he shall apply sufficiently in
advance before the expiry of the leave to the employer, who shall send a written reply either
granting or refusing extension of leave.

title: Payment of wages for unveiled leave
text:
If the services of a worker, to whom any annual leave is
due, is dispensed with whether as a result of retrenchment, discharge, removal, dismissal,
termination, retirement or by reason of his resignation before he has availed of any such leave, the
employer shall pay his wages in lieu of the unveiled leave at the rate he is entitled to during the
period of leave.

title: Stoppage of work
text:
(1) The employer may, at any time, in the event of fire, catastrophe,
breakdown of machinery, or stoppage of power supply, epidemics, civil commotion or any other
cause beyond his control, stop any section or sections of the establishment, wholly or partly.
(2)-(4) The employer shall notify affected workers by notice posted on the notice board, indicating
when work will resume.
(5) Workers directed to stay at their place of work following such stoppage may not be paid for the
period of detention if it does not exceed one hour, and shall be paid wages for the whole period of
detention if it exceeds one hour.
(6) If the period of stoppage does not exceed one working day, a worker may not be paid any wages.
(7) If the period of stoppage continues for more than a working day, a worker affected, other than a
casual or badli worker, shall be paid wages for the day or days by which it exceeds one working day.
(8) If the period of stoppage extends beyond three working days, the workers may be laid-off in
accordance with section 16.

title: Closure of establishment
text:
(1) The employer may, in the event of an illegal strike by any section
or department of any establishment, close down either wholly or partly such section or department
and the workers who participated in the illegal strike shall not be paid any wages for such closure.
(2) Where such closing affects another section or department so that it is not possible to keep it
open, that section may also be closed and the workers affected shall be paid wages as in the case of
lay-off for a period of three days and thereafter no wages for such closure.
(3) The fact of such closure and of resumption of work shall be notified by notice on the notice
board.

title: Calculation of 'one year', 'six months' and 'wages' in certain cases
text:
(1) A worker who, during
the preceding twelve calendar months, has actually worked for not less than two hundred and forty
days (or one hundred and twenty days for 'six months') shall be deemed to have completed 'one
year' or 'six months' of continuous service.
(2) Days on which a worker has been laid-off, on leave with or without wages due to sickness or
accident, on legal strike or out of work due to illegal lock-out, or (for female workers) on maternity
leave not exceeding sixteen weeks, shall be counted for this purpose.
(3) For the purpose of calculating compensation under sections 19, 20 or 23 or wages under sections
22, 23, 26, or 27, 'wages' shall mean the average of the basic wages and dearness allowance and
ad-hoc or interim pay, if any, paid to the worker during the twelve months immediately preceding
the date of his retrenchment, dismissal, removal, discharge, retirement or termination of employment.

title: Restrictions of application of sections 12, 16, 17, and 18
text:
The provisions of sections 12, 16,
17, and 18 shall not apply to any establishment in which five or more workers are not employed, or
were not employed on any day of the preceding twelve months.

title: Right of laid-off workers for compensation
text:
(1) A worker, other than a badli or casual worker,
whose name is on the muster-rolls and who has completed not less than one year of continuous
service, when laid-off, shall be paid compensation for all days during which he is laid-off, except
weekly holidays.
(2) The compensation shall be equal to half of the total of basic wages and dearness allowance, and
ad-hoc or interim pay, if any, and the full amount of housing allowance, if any.
(3) A badli worker who has completed one year of continuous service ceases to be regarded as
'badli' for this section.
(4) No worker shall, unless agreed otherwise, be entitled to compensation under this section for
more than forty-five days during any calendar year.
(5)-(6) If a worker is laid-off for more than forty-five days in a calendar year, subsequent periods of
fifteen days or more are compensated at one-fourth of the total of basic wages and dearness
allowance, and ad-hoc or interim pay, plus full housing allowance, if any.
(7) The employer may instead retrench such a worker under section 20.

title: Muster-roll for laid-off workers
text:
The employer shall maintain a muster-roll for laid-off
workers who present themselves for work at the appointed time during normal working hours.

title: Laid-off workers not entitled to compensation in certain cases
text:
No compensation is payable
to a laid-off worker who refuses alternative employment on the same wages not requiring special
skill, in the same or a nearby establishment of the same employer, or who does not present himself
for work when required.

title: Death benefit
text:
If a worker dies while in service after continuous service of not less than three
years, his nominee (or dependant, in the absence of a nominee) shall be paid compensation at the
rate of thirty days' wages for every completed year of service, or gratuity if any, whichever is
higher, in addition to other benefits, unless a compulsory insurance scheme or chapter XII
compensation applies, in which case whichever is higher shall be paid.

title: Retrenchment
text:
(1) A worker may be retrenched from service on the ground of redundancy.
(2) No worker with not less than one year of continuous service shall be retrenched unless given one
month's notice in writing (or paid in lieu), a copy sent to the chief Inspector and the collective
bargaining agent, and paid compensation equivalent to thirty days' wages or gratuity, whichever is
higher, for every completed year of service.
(3) In the case of retrenchment under section 16(7), no notice is necessary, but the worker shall be
paid fifteen days' wages in addition to the compensation or gratuity payable under sub-section
(2)(c).
(4) Where a category of workers is to be retrenched, absent agreement otherwise, the employer shall
retrench the worker last employed in that category (last-in-first-out).

title: Re-employment of retrenched workers
text:
Where the employer proposes to re-employ within one
year of retrenchment, retrenched workers of that category shall be given the first opportunity, in
order of length of service.

title: Discharge from service
text:
(1) A worker may be discharged for reasons of physical or mental
incapacity or continued ill-health certified by a registered medical practitioner.
(2) A worker with not less than one year of continuous service so discharged shall be paid
compensation at the rate of thirty days' wages for every completed year of service, or gratuity if any,
whichever is higher.

title: Punishment for conviction and misconduct
text:
(1) A worker may be dismissed without prior
notice or pay in lieu if convicted of a criminal offence or found guilty of misconduct under section

title: (2) Instead of dismissal, lesser punishments may be awarded
text:
removal; reduction to a lower
post/grade/pay for up to one year; stoppage of promotion for up to one year; withholding of
increment for up to one year; fine; suspension without wages for up to seven days; or censure/
warning.
(3) A worker dismissed or removed as punishment, if continuous service is not less than one year,
shall be paid compensation at the rate of fourteen days' wages for every completed year of service,
or gratuity if any, whichever is higher — except no compensation is payable for misconduct
specified in sub-section (4)(b).
(4) Misconduct includes: wilful insubordination or disobedience; theft, fraud or dishonesty; taking or
giving bribes; habitual late attendance; habitual breach of law/rule/regulation; riotous or disorderly
behaviour; habitual negligence of work; habitual breach of any approved rule of employment; and
falsifying or damaging employer's official records.
(5) If a worker dismissed under sub-section (1)(a) is acquitted on appeal, he shall be reinstated
without back wages, or paid compensation as on discharge if reinstatement is not possible.

title: Special provisions relating to fine
text:
(1) No fine exceeding one-tenth of wages payable for a
wage-period may be imposed in that period.
(2) No fine shall be imposed on a worker under fifteen years of age.
(3) No fine shall be recovered by instalments or after sixty days from imposition.
(4)-(5) Fines are deemed imposed on the day of the offence, and all fines must be recorded in a
prescribed register and applied only to purposes beneficial to workers.

title: Termination of employment by employers otherwise than by dismissal etc.
text:
(1) A
permanent worker's employment may be terminated by giving 120 days' notice (monthly-rated) or
60 days' notice (other workers), in writing.
(2) A temporary worker's employment (not due to completion of the temporary work) may be
terminated with 30 days' notice (monthly-rated) or 14 days' notice (other workers).
(3) Termination without notice is permitted if wages are paid in lieu of the notice period.
(4) A terminated permanent worker shall be paid compensation at the rate of thirty days' wages for
every completed year of service, or gratuity if any, whichever is higher, plus other entitled benefits.

title: Termination of employment by workers
text:
(1) A permanent worker may resign by giving sixty
days' written notice.
(2) A temporary worker may resign by giving thirty days' notice (monthly-rated) or fourteen days'
notice (other workers).
(3) Resignation without notice is permitted if wages are paid in lieu of the notice period.
(4) A resigning permanent worker shall be paid compensation at fourteen days' wages per completed
year of service (five to under ten years of continuous service) or thirty days' wages per completed
year (ten years or more), or gratuity if any, whichever is higher.

title: Retirement of worker
text:
(1) A worker shall retire from employment on completion of the
fifty-seventh year of age.
(2) The date of birth recorded in the service book is conclusive proof of age.
(3) Every retiring worker shall be paid the benefits due under section 26(4) or the establishment's
own service rules.
(4) The appropriate authority may afterwards re-employ the retiring worker under contract.

title: Payment of Provident Fund
text:
No worker who is a member of a provident fund shall be deprived,
due to retrenchment, dismissal, removal, discharge or termination, of the benefit of the fund
including the employer's contribution, if entitled under the fund's rules.

title: Time limit of final payment of workers
text:
Where employment ceases due to retirement,
discharge, retrenchment, dismissal or termination, all amounts due shall be paid within a maximum
of thirty working days.

title: Certificate of service
text:
Every worker, other than casual or badli, is entitled to a certificate of
service on retrenchment, discharge, dismissal, removal, retirement or termination.

title: Eviction from residential accommodation
text:
(1) A worker occupying employer-provided
residential accommodation whose service has ceased shall vacate within sixty days.
(2)-(5) On default, the employer may apply to the Labour Court, which may order eviction, if
necessary by police, after giving at least six hours' notice to occupants.

title: Grievance procedure
text:
(1) A worker with a grievance under this chapter shall submit it in
writing to the employer by registered post within thirty days of the cause arising.
(2) The employer shall enquire, give a hearing, and communicate a decision in writing within
fifteen days of receipt.
(3) If the employer fails to decide, or the worker is dissatisfied, the worker may complain to the
Labour Court within thirty days.
(4)-(5) The Labour Court shall hear the parties and may order relief including reinstatement, with or
without back wages, or convert a dismissal/removal/discharge order to a lesser punishment under
section 23(2).
(6) Appeal from a Labour Court order lies to the Tribunal within thirty days, and the Tribunal's
decision is final.
(7)-(9) No court fees are payable; a complaint is not a prosecution; and no complaint lies against a
termination under section 26 unless it is alleged to be motivated by trade union activities or the
worker was deprived of the benefits specified in that section.

CHAPTER III
EMPLOYMENT OF ADOLESCENT

title: Prohibition of employment of children and adolescent
text:
(1) No child shall be employed or
permitted to work in any occupation or establishment.
(2) No adolescent shall be employed or permitted to work unless a certificate of fitness from a
registered medical practitioner is held by the employer, and the adolescent carries a token referring
to it while at work.
(3) This does not apply to an adolescent employed as an apprentice or for vocational training.
(4) The Government may, in an emergency, suspend the certificate requirement by notification.

title: Prohibition of certain agreement in respect of children
text:
No parent or guardian of a child shall
make an agreement to allow the child's services to be utilised in any employment.

title: Disputes as to age
text:
(1) A dispute as to whether a person is a child or adolescent shall, absent a
certificate, be referred to a registered medical practitioner for decision.
(2) Such a medical certificate is conclusive evidence of age.

title: Certificate of fitness
text:
(1) A registered medical practitioner shall, on application, examine and
certify whether an adolescent is fit to work in an occupation or establishment.
(2) A certificate of fitness is valid for twelve months from issue.
(3) The fee is payable by the employer, not the adolescent or guardian.

title: Power to require medical examination
text:
An Inspector who believes a working person is an
adolescent without a fitness certificate, or that a certified adolescent is no longer fit, may require
that the adolescent not work until examined and certified.

title: Restriction of employment of adolescent in certain work
text:
No adolescent shall clean, lubricate
or adjust machinery in motion, or work between moving parts of machinery in motion.

title: Employment of adolescent on dangerous machines
text:
No adolescent shall work at a dangerous
machine unless fully instructed on the dangers and precautions, and either sufficiently trained or
under adequate supervision.

title: Working hours for adolescent
text:
(1) No adolescent shall work more than five hours a day or
thirty hours a week in a factory or mine.
(2) No adolescent shall work more than seven hours a day or forty-two hours a week in any other
establishment.
(3) No adolescent shall work between 7.00 p.m. and 7.00 a.m.
(4) With overtime, total hours shall not exceed thirty-six hours a week (factory/mine) or forty-eight
hours a week (other establishments).
(5) An adolescent's work shall be limited to two non-overlapping shifts of not more than seven and a
half hours each.
(6) An adolescent shall be employed in only one relay, changeable no more than once every thirty
days without the Inspector's permission.
(7) Weekly holiday provisions apply to adolescent workers without exemption.
(8) No adolescent shall work in more than one establishment in a day.

title: Prohibition of employment of adolescent in underground and under-water work
text:
No
adolescent shall be employed in underground or underwater work.

title: Notice of periods of work for adolescent
text:
(1)-(4) Every establishment employing adolescents
shall display a notice of their specified working periods, fixed in the same manner as for adult
workers.

title: Exception in certain cases of employment of children
text:
(1) A child who has completed twelve
years of age may be employed in light work that does not endanger health, development, or
interfere with education (school hours must be protected).
(2) Provisions applicable to adolescents apply, with necessary modification, to such child workers.

CHAPTER IV
MATERNITY BENEFIT

title: Employment of women workers prohibited during certain period
text:
(1)-(2) No employer
shall knowingly employ, and no woman shall work, during the eight weeks immediately following
delivery.
(3) No employer shall assign arduous work, long standing, or health-risking work to a woman
believed to be within ten weeks of delivery, or within ten weeks after delivery — except tea
plantation workers certified fit for light work by the estate's medical practitioner, who must be paid
the prevailing rate for that work in addition to maternity benefit.

title: Right to, and liability for, payment of maternity benefit
text:
(1) Every woman employed is
entitled to, and her employer liable for, maternity benefit for eight weeks preceding and eight weeks
following the expected day of delivery, provided she has worked at least six months immediately
preceding the day of delivery.
(2) No maternity benefit is payable if, at confinement, she has two or more surviving children (but
she remains entitled to the leave).

title: Procedure regarding payment of maternity benefit
text:
(1)-(2) A pregnant woman shall give
notice (oral or written) that she expects confinement within eight weeks, and may nominate a person
to receive payment in case of her death; if she has not given prior notice, she must give notice within
seven days of delivery.
(3) On notice, the employer shall permit her to be absent from work through eight weeks after
delivery.
(4) The employer shall pay maternity benefit in instalments tied to a medical certificate and proof of
birth, as the woman elects among the specified payment schedules; proof must be produced within
three months of delivery.
(5) Acceptable proof includes a certified birth-register extract or a registered medical practitioner's
certificate.

title: Amount of maternity benefit
text:
(1)-(2) Maternity benefit is payable at the daily, weekly or
monthly average wage, calculated by dividing total wages earned in the three months immediately
preceding the notice by the number of days actually worked, paid wholly in cash.

title: Payment of maternity benefit in case of a woman's death
text:
(1) If a woman entitled to
maternity benefit dies at delivery or within the following eight months, the employer shall pay the
benefit to whoever cares for the surviving child, or, if the child does not survive, to her nominee or
legal representative.
(2) If she dies during the entitlement period before giving birth, the employer's liability is limited to
the period up to her death; the balance is paid to her nominee or legal representative.

title: Restriction on termination of employment of a woman in certain cases
text:
A notice or order of
discharge, dismissal, removal or termination given to a woman within six months before or eight
weeks after her delivery, without sufficient cause, does not deprive her of maternity benefit she
would otherwise be entitled to.

CHAPTER V
HEALTH AND HYGIENE

title: Cleanliness
text:
Every establishment shall be kept clean and free from effluvia, with daily removal
of dirt/refuse, weekly floor washing, drainage where floors become wet, and periodic repainting/
whitewashing of walls and ceilings (at least once every three years if painted/varnished, or every
fourteen months if whitewashed), with dates of such work recorded in a prescribed register.

title: Ventilation and temperature
text:
Every establishment shall maintain adequate ventilation and a
temperature that secures reasonable comfort and prevents injury to health, with measures to isolate
or reduce excessive heat from manufacturing processes.

title: Dust and fume
text:
Effective measures shall prevent accumulation and inhalation of injurious dust
or fume in work-rooms, including exhaust appliances near the point of origin; internal combustion
engines must vent exhaust outdoors or otherwise prevent harmful fume accumulation.

title: Disposal of wastes and effluents
text:
Effective arrangements shall be made for disposal of wastes
and effluents from the manufacturing process.

title: Artificial humidification
text:
Where humidity is artificially increased, the water used must come
from a public supply or be effectively purified; an Inspector may order specific purification
measures.

title: Overcrowding
text:
(1)-(2) No work-room shall be overcrowded to a degree injurious to health; at
least 9.5 cubic metres of space per worker is required (space above 4.25 metres from the floor is
excluded).
(3)-(4) The chief Inspector may require posted notices of maximum occupancy, or exempt a
work-room where compliance is unnecessary for health.

title: Lighting
text:
Sufficient and suitable lighting (natural or artificial) shall be provided; windows/
skylights kept clean; glare and shadow causing eye strain or accident risk shall be prevented.

title: Drinking water
text:
(1)-(4) Wholesome drinking water shall be provided at suitable points, marked
'Drinking water' in Bangla; establishments with 250 or more workers must provide for cooling
drinking water in hot weather; oral rehydration therapy must be available where heat-related
dehydration risk exists near machinery.

title: Latrines and urinals
text:
Sufficient, conveniently located, separately provided (by sex), well-lit,
ventilated, and hygienically maintained latrines and urinals are required in every establishment.

title: Dust bin and spittoon
text:
(1)-(3) Sufficient dust bins and spittoons shall be provided and kept
clean; no person shall litter or spit outside them; the relevant notice and penalty must be displayed.

CHAPTER VI
SAFETY

title: Safety of building and machinery
text:
(1)-(2) An Inspector who finds a building, way, machinery
or plant dangerous to life or safety may order remedial measures by a specified date, or prohibit its
use until repaired if the danger is imminent.

title: Precaution in case of fire
text:
(1) Every establishment shall have at least one alternative stairway
per floor and prescribed means of escape and fire-fighting apparatus.
(2) An Inspector may order compliance by a specified date.
(3)-(6) Exit doors must open easily from inside (and generally outward), be unobstructed, clearly
marked in Bangla with red lettering, and a free passageway to each escape route must be maintained.
(7)-(8) Establishments with more than ten workers above ground floor, or storing explosive/
inflammable materials, must ensure workers are trained in escape routines; factories with fifty or
more workers must hold a mock fire drill at least annually and keep records.

title: Fencing of machinery
text:
(1)-(2) Moving parts of prime movers, flywheels, transmission
machinery, and other dangerous machine parts must be securely fenced unless inherently as safe
unfenced; set screws, bolts, gearing etc. that could cause contact injury must also be fenced.

title: Work on or near machinery in motion
text:
(1) Examination, lubrication or adjustment of
machinery in motion may only be performed by a specially trained adult male worker in tight-fitting
clothing, recorded in a prescribed register, following belt-handling safety limits.
(2) The Government may prohibit cleaning/lubricating/adjusting specified machine parts while in
motion.

title: Striking gear and devices for cutting off power
text:
(1)-(2) Suitable striking gear for driving
belts, and devices for cutting off power in emergencies, must be provided and maintained in every
work-room.

title: Self-acting machines
text:
No traversing part of a self-acting machine, or material carried on it,
shall be allowed to run within forty-five centimetres of a fixed structure where a person might pass,
subject to a grandfather exemption the chief Inspector may permit for pre-existing machines.

title: Casing of new machinery
text:
In machinery installed after the Act's commencement, set screws,
bolts and gearing must be sunk, encased or guarded to prevent danger, unless as safe unencased.

title: Cranes and other lifting machinery
text:
Lifting machinery must be of good construction and
sound material, properly maintained, examined by a competent person at least every twelve months
with records kept; must not be loaded beyond its marked safe working load; and effective measures
must keep a travelling crane at least six metres from workers on its wheel-track.

title: Hoists and lifts
text:
(1)-(7) Hoists and lifts must be of good construction, properly maintained, and
examined at least every six months with records kept; enclosed to prevent trapping; marked with
maximum safe load; fitted with interlocking gates; and (for those installed after the Act) fitted with
at least two independently attached ropes/chains, a device to support the cage if ropes break, and an
automatic anti-over-running device, subject to a chief Inspector exemption for pre-existing
installations.

title: Revolving machinery
text:
(1)-(3) Grinding rooms must display notices of maximum safe peripheral
speed, shaft speed, and pulley diameter; these speeds must not be exceeded; and safety measures for
revolving vessels/wheels driven by power must be maintained.

title: Pressure plant
text:
Where plant or machinery operates above atmospheric pressure, effective
measures shall ensure the safe working pressure is not exceeded.

title: Floors, stairs and means of access
text:
All floors, stairs, passages and gangways must be soundly
constructed, properly maintained, fitted with handrails where necessary for safety, and kept clean,
wide and clear of obstructions, with safe means of access to every workplace.

title: Pits, sumps, opening in floors, etc.
text:
Fixed vessels, sumps, tanks, pits or floor openings that are
a source of danger must be securely covered or fenced.

title: Excessive weights
text:
No person shall be required to lift, carry or move a load so heavy as to be
likely to cause injury.

title: Protection of eyes
text:
The Government may require effective screens or goggles for workers
exposed to risk of eye injury from particles, fragments, excessive light or heat in a manufacturing
process.

title: Powers to require specifications of defective parts or tests of stability
text:
An Inspector who
believes a building, way, machinery or plant may be dangerous may require drawings, specifications
or stability tests by a specified date.

title: Precaution against dangerous fumes
text:
(1)-(5) Entry into confined spaces with dangerous fumes
is restricted to persons with proper manholes/egress, prohibited portable lighting above 24 volts,
required fume clearance or breathing apparatus with a safety rope attended from outside, mandatory
availability and periodic certification of breathing/reviving apparatus, and mandatory cooling/
ventilation before entering boilers, furnaces or similar confined spaces.

title: Explosive or inflammable dust, gas, etc.
text:
(1)-(4) Where a process produces explosive dust, gas,
fume or vapour, practicable measures must prevent explosion via enclosure, removal of
accumulation, and exclusion of ignition sources; plant not built to withstand explosion pressure must
have measures to restrict spread; pressurised explosive/inflammable plant may only be opened under
specified depressurisation and re-securing procedures; and welding/cutting operations on vessels that
held explosive substances require the substance and fumes to be removed first and adequate cooling
before further use.

CHAPTER VII
SPECIAL PROVISIONS RELATING TO HEALTH, HYGIENE AND SAFETY

title: Dangerous operations
text:
Where an operation exposes workers to serious risk of bodily injury,
poisoning or disease, the Government may make rules declaring it hazardous, restricting employment
of women/adolescents/children in it, requiring periodic medical examination and fitness
certification, providing protection for persons in or near the operation, and requiring notices on
corrosive chemical precautions.

title: Notice to be given of accidents
text:
(1) An employer must notify the Inspector within two working
days of any accident causing loss of life or bodily injury, or of any accidental explosion, ignition,
fire, or irruption of water/fumes in the establishment.
(2) Where the accident causes bodily injury resulting in compulsory absence from work, further
notice and reporting requirements apply (text of this sub-section continues beyond the currently
ingested extract).

title: Notice of certain dangerous occurrences
text: Where there occurs in any establishment any dangerous occurrence causing bodily injury, disability or risk, the employer or manager shall immediately send notice in the prescribed form to the Inspector.

title: Notice of certain disease
text: (1) Where any worker contracts any disease specified in the Second Schedule, the manager shall send notice to the Chief Inspector. (2) Any attending medical practitioner shall report the worker's details and disease to the Chief Inspector.

title: Power to direct inquiry into cases of accident or disease
text: The Government may appoint a competent person to inquire into any accident or disease occurring in an establishment and report on its causes and circumstances.

title: Power to take samples
text: An Inspector may take samples of any substance used or intended to be used in an establishment which he believes to be dangerous or toxic.

title: Powers of Inspector in case of imminent danger
text: If an Inspector considers any building, machinery or process dangerous to human life or safety, he may order the employer in writing to prohibit use until repaired or guarded.

title: Notice of opening of establishment
text: An employer shall send a written notice to the Chief Inspector at least 30 days before commencing work in any manufacturing or industrial establishment.

title: Dangerous operations
text: Where any process exposes workers to serious risk of bodily injury or disease, the Government may make rules declaring it hazardous and specifying protective measures.

title: Safety record book
text:
In every establishment employing fifty or more workers, a safety record book shall be maintained in the prescribed format.

CHAPTER VIII
WELFARE

title: First-aid appliances
text: (1) There shall be provided and maintained first-aid boxes or cupboards equipped with prescribed contents. (2) At least one first-aid box shall be maintained for every 150 workers. (3) Each first-aid box shall be kept in charge of a trained person available during working hours.

title: Maintenance of safety record book
text: Employers in establishments employing 50 or more workers shall maintain a safety record book and safety committee.

title: Washing facilities
text: In every establishment adequate and suitable facilities for washing shall be provided and maintained for the use of workers.

title: Canteens
text: (1) In any establishment wherein more than 100 workers are ordinarily employed, an adequate canteen shall be provided and maintained for the use of workers.

title: Shelters, rest-rooms and lunch-rooms
text: (1) In every establishment wherein more than 50 workers are ordinarily employed, adequate and suitable shelters or rest-rooms and lunch-rooms with drinking water shall be provided.

title: Rooms for children (Creche)
text: (1) In every establishment wherein 40 or more female workers are ordinarily employed, a suitable room or rooms shall be provided for the use of children under six years of age.

title: Recreational and educational facilities in tea plantations
text: Employers in tea gardens shall provide recreational, medical and primary educational facilities for workers and their children.

title: Medical care for tea plantation workers
text: Employers in tea gardens shall provide medical facilities and emergency care for resident workers and their families.

title: Housing facilities in tea plantations
text: Employers in tea gardens shall provide housing accommodation for resident workers and their families.

title: Facilities for daily necessities in tea plantations
text: Employers in tea gardens shall provide facilities for supply of daily food grain and essential commodities to workers.

title: Compulsory group insurance
text:
(1) In establishments where 100 or more permanent workers are employed, the employer shall introduce compulsory group insurance scheme for workers.

CHAPTER IX
WORKING HOURS AND LEAVE

title: Daily working hours
text: No adult worker shall ordinarily be required or allowed to work in an establishment for more than eight hours in any day. Provided that subject to Section 108, a worker may work up to ten hours a day.

title: Interval for rest or meal
text: No worker shall be required to work for more than six hours continuously without an interval of at least one hour for rest or meal.

title: Weekly working hours
text: (1) No adult worker shall ordinarily be required or allowed to work for more than forty-eight hours in any week. (2) Total working hours inclusive of overtime shall not exceed sixty hours in any week and average fifty-six hours per week on annual basis.

title: Weekly holiday
text: An adult worker in an establishment shall be allowed in each week at least one whole day holiday (or one and a half day holiday in commercial establishments).

title: Compensatory weekly holiday
text: Where a worker is deprived of any weekly holiday due to emergency work, he shall be allowed compensatory holidays within the next two months.

title: Spreadover
text: The period of work of an adult worker inclusive of intervals for rest shall not spread over more than eleven hours in any day.

title: Night shift work
text: Where a worker works on a night shift extending beyond midnight, a holiday for a whole day shall mean a period of 24 consecutive hours beginning when his shift ends.

title: Restriction on double employment
text: No worker shall work in more than one establishment on any day without written permission.

title: Extra allowance for overtime
text: Where a worker works in an establishment for more than eight hours in any day or forty-eight hours in any week, he shall be entitled to overtime allowance at twice the rate of his basic wages and dear allowance.

title: Restriction on working hours of female workers
text: No female worker shall without her consent be required to work between 10:00 PM and 6:00 AM.

title: Display of notice of periods of work
text: Notice of working hours, shifts and rest intervals shall be conspicuously displayed in every establishment.

title: Casual leave
text: Every worker shall be entitled to casual leave with full wages for ten days in a calendar year.

title: Sick leave
text: (1) Every worker shall be entitled to sick leave with full wages for fourteen days in a calendar year on medical certificate.

title: Annual leave with wages
text: Every adult worker who has completed one year of continuous service shall be allowed annual leave with full wages at the rate of one day for every 18 days of work (factory/shop) or one day for every 22 days of work (tea plantation).

title: Festival holiday
text: Every worker shall be allowed eleven days of paid festival holidays in a calendar year.

title: Payment of wages during leave or holiday period
text: For leave or holidays allowed under Sections 111-114, a worker shall be paid at the rate equal to the daily average of his full wages.

title: Advance payment of wages in certain cases
text: A worker allowed leave for not less than four days shall be paid wages due for the leave period before his leave begins.

title: Unavailed leave encashable
text: Earned annual leave not availed by a worker may be accumulated up to 40 days (factory) or 60 days (shop) and encashed at retirement or termination.

title: Power to exempt establishments from Chapter IX
text: The Government may by notification exempt any establishment or class of establishments from provisions of working hours in public emergency.

title: Power to make rules regarding leave and hours
text:
The Government may make rules regulating overtime, working hours, leave registers and notices.

CHAPTER X
WAGES AND PAYMENT THEREOF

title: Responsibility for payment of wages
text: Every employer shall be responsible for the payment to workers employed by him of all wages required to be paid under this Act.

title: Fixation of wage-periods
text: Every person responsible for the payment of wages shall fix wage periods not exceeding one month.

title: Time of payment of wages
text: Wages of every worker shall be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the last day of the wage-period.

title: Wages to be paid in current coin or currency notes
text: All wages shall be paid in current currency notes or bank coins, or directly credited to worker's bank account or digital payment account.

title: Deductions which may be made from wages
text: No deductions shall be made from the wages of a worker except those authorized under this Act (fines, absence from duty, damage to goods, housing, provident fund, tax).

title: Deductions for absence from duty
text: Deductions may be made for absence from duty for the period the worker was absent.

title: Deductions for damage or loss
text: Deductions for damage or loss of goods expressly entrusted to worker shall not exceed the actual damage caused.

title: Deductions for services rendered
text: Deductions may be made for house accommodation or amenity provided by employer.

title: Deductions for recovery of advances
text: Recovery of advances of money given before employment shall be made from the first payment of wages.

title: Deductions for provident fund and co-operative societies
text: Deductions may be made for provident fund contributions or co-operative society loans authorized by worker.

title: Claims arising out of deductions or delay in payment
text: Where unpaid wages or unauthorized deductions occur, worker or trade union may apply to Labour Court.

title: Power of Labour Court to direct payment
text: The Labour Court after hearing may order repayment of delayed wages together with compensation up to ten times the amount.

title: Execution of order of Labour Court
text: Any sum ordered by Labour Court to be paid under Section 131 may be recovered as a public demand or fine.

title: Appeal against order of Labour Court
text: An appeal against an order of Labour Court under Section 131 lies to the Labour Appellate Tribunal within 30 days.

title: Bar of suits
text: No court shall entertain any suit for the recovery of wages in so far as the sum claimed could have been recovered by application under Section 130.

title: Minimum Wage Board
text: The Government shall establish a Minimum Wage Board consisting of Chairman, independent member, employer representative, and worker representative.

title: Recommendation of minimum rates of wages
text: Minimum Wage Board shall upon reference by Government recommend minimum rates of wages for workers in specified industries.

title: Factors to be considered in recommending minimum wages
text: Board shall consider cost of living, standard of living, production cost, productivity, and capacity of industry.

title: Declaration of minimum rates of wages
text: The Government may by notification declare the minimum rates of wages recommended by Minimum Wage Board.

title: Minimum wages to be binding
text: Minimum wages declared by Government shall be binding on all employers in the industry concerned; paying less than minimum wage is an offence.

title: Periodic review of minimum rates of wages
text: Minimum rates of wages shall be reviewed every five years by the Minimum Wage Board.

title: Prohibition of paying less than minimum wage
text: No employer shall pay any worker wages at a rate lower than the declared minimum rate of wages.

title: Worker's right to receive minimum wages
text: Every worker shall be entitled to receive minimum wages declared under Section 138 regardless of any contract to the contrary.

title: Payment of equal wages for equal work
text: No discrimination shall be made between male and female workers in fixing rates of wages for work of equal value.

title: Wage Board for tea plantation workers
text: Specialized wage board provisions apply to tea garden workers and maritime workers.

title: Newspaper workers wage board
text: Specialized Newspaper Wage Board recommendations govern wages of working journalists and newspaper employees.

title: Implementation of Newspaper Wage Board award
text: Newspaper employers must implement tribunal awards within specified timelines.

title: Power to make rules under Chapter X
text: Government may make rules for wage registers, wage slips, and Minimum Wage Board procedures.

title: Display of wage rates
text: Employers shall display minimum wage rates conspicuously at place of work.

title: Exemption from wage payment provisions
text:
Government may exempt specialized temporary emergency operations from certain wage rules.

CHAPTER XI
WORKERS' COMPENSATION FOR INJURY BY ACCIDENT

title: Employer's liability for compensation
text: (1) If personal injury is caused to a worker by accident arising out of and in the course of his employment, his employer shall be liable to pay compensation. (2) Employer is exempt if injury does not disable worker for more than three days, or if caused by intoxication or willful disobedience of safety rules.

title: Amount of compensation
text: Compensation payable for death shall be a lump sum prescribed in the Fifth Schedule (or statutory minimum), and for permanent total disablement a lump sum prescribed therein.

title: Method of calculating monthly wages for compensation
text: Monthly wages shall be calculated based on average monthly earnings of worker in twelve months prior to accident.

title: Review of monthly payments
text: Any half-monthly payment payable under this Chapter may be reviewed by Commissioner on application of employer or worker.

title: Commutation of half-monthly payments
text: Any right to receive half-monthly payments may by agreement or order of Commissioner be redeemed by a lump sum.

title: Distribution of compensation
text: Compensation for death shall be deposited with Commissioner and distributed among dependents.

title: Notice and claim of accident
text: No claim for compensation shall be entertained unless notice of accident is given to employer as soon as practicable.

title: Medical examination
text: A worker giving notice of accident shall submit himself for medical examination by qualified medical practitioner provided by employer.

title: Contracting out prohibited
text: Any contract or agreement whereby a worker relinquishes right to compensation from employer shall be null and void.

title: Compensation to be first charge on assets
text: Compensation payable by employer shall rank prior to all other debts in bankruptcy or liquidation.

title: Insolvency of employer
text: Where employer becomes insolvent, rights against insurer transfer to and vest in worker.

title: Special provisions relating to seamen and maritime workers
text: Compensation claims for accidents at sea may be served on master of ship or owner.

title: Compensation for occupational disease
text: Contracting of specified occupational diseases (Pneumoconiosis, Lead poisoning, Silicosis) shall be deemed injury by accident.

title: Returns as to compensation
text: Every employer shall send annual return to Commissioner showing number of injuries and compensation paid.

title: Appointment of Commissioners for Workers' Compensation
text: Government may appoint qualified persons to be Commissioners for Workers' Compensation.

title: Functions of Commissioners
text: All claims for compensation, liability, and settlement shall be determined by Commissioner.

title: Form of application to Commissioner
text: Applications to Commissioner shall be filed in prescribed form with details of injury and claim.

title: Power of Commissioner to require further deposit
text: Commissioner may require employer to deposit additional compensation if initial deposit is insufficient.

title: Powers and procedure of Commissioners
text: Commissioner shall have powers of Civil Court for enforcing attendance of witnesses and production of documents.

title: Appearance of parties
text: Parties may appear before Commissioner in person, by legal practitioner, or by authorized trade union officer.

title: Method of recording evidence
text: Evidence before Commissioner shall be taken down in writing and form part of record.

title: Costs of proceedings
text: Costs of any proceeding before Commissioner shall be in discretion of Commissioner.

title: Registration of agreements
text: Memorandum of agreement for lump sum compensation must be submitted to Commissioner for registration.

title: Effect of failure to register agreement
text: Unregistered agreement for lump sum payment shall not exempt employer from liability.

title: Appeals against Commissioner's order
text:
Appeal lies to Labour Appellate Tribunal against Commissioner's order within sixty days.

CHAPTER XII
TRADE UNIONS AND INDUSTRIAL RELATIONS

title: Right of workers and employers to form trade unions
text: Workers and employers without distinction shall have right to establish and join trade unions of their choice.

title: Registration of trade unions
text: Any trade union may apply for registration under this Chapter to Registrar of Trade Unions.

title: Application for registration
text: Application for registration shall be made in prescribed form signed by President and Secretary of trade union.

title: Requirements for registration
text: (1) A trade union of workers shall not be registered unless it has minimum membership of 20% of total workers employed in establishment.

title: Disqualification for membership of trade union
text: A person convicted of moral turpitude or offence under Section 304 shall be disqualified from union officer post.

title: Registered trade union to maintain constitution
text: Constitution of registered trade union shall provide name, objects, fund usage, election of officers, and executive committee structure.

title: Power of Registrar to register or refuse registration
text: Registrar shall register trade union within 55 days if requirements met, or issue reasoned refusal.

title: Cancellation of registration
text: Registrar may cancel registration of trade union if union obtained registration by fraud or violated Act provisions.

title: Appeal against refusal or cancellation of registration
text: Any person aggrieved by refusal or cancellation of registration may appeal to Labour Court within 30 days.

title: Trade union of tea garden and sea workers
text: Specialized union registration provisions apply to tea gardens and maritime sectors.

title: Collective Bargaining Agent (CBA)
text: (1) Registered trade union with majority support shall be certified as Collective Bargaining Agent for establishment.

title: Secret ballot for CBA determination
text: Where more than one trade union exists in establishment, Registrar shall conduct secret ballot to determine CBA.

title: Functions of Collective Bargaining Agent
text: CBA shall undertake collective bargaining on terms of employment, represent workers in disputes, and nominate representatives to welfare bodies.

title: Rights of CBA
text: CBA may collect union subscriptions, display notices on board, and represent workers in grievance and court proceedings.

title: Federation of trade unions
text: Two or more registered trade unions in same industry may form a Federation of Trade Unions.

title: Immunity from civil suit in certain cases
text: No civil suit or legal proceeding shall lie against registered trade union or its officers for acts done in furtherance of industrial dispute.

title: Enforceability of agreement
text: An agreement between trade union and employer shall be legally binding on parties and workers represented.

title: Maintenance of list of members and account books
text: Every registered trade union shall maintain membership register, minute book, and audited account books.

title: Submission of annual returns
text: Every registered trade union shall send annual audited financial return to Registrar before 30th April.

title: Unfair labour practices on part of employers
text: Employer shall not discriminate, threaten, dismiss or interfere with worker for trade union activities.

title: Unfair labour practices on part of workers or trade unions
text: Worker or trade union shall not coerce, intimidate, compel employer or conduct illegal strike.

title: Protection of trade union leaders during registration
text: Pending application for registration, no officer of trade union shall be transferred or dismissed without Registrar permission.

title: Dual membership prohibited
text: No worker shall be member of more than one trade union at same time in same establishment.

title: Trade union funds usage
text: Funds of registered trade union shall be spent only for objects authorized under its constitution.

title: Check-off
text: Employer shall upon written authorization of worker deduct trade union subscription from wages and remit to CBA.

title: Participation in international labor bodies
text: Registered trade unions may affiliate with international worker organizations.

title: Right of inspection of union books
text: Officers and members of trade union may inspect union membership register and account books.

title: Determination of CBA in multi-unit establishment
text: Registrar shall designate master CBA for multi-plant or multi-unit establishments.

title: Redressal against unfair labor practice
text: Party aggrieved by unfair labor practice under Section 194 or 195 may apply to Labour Court.

title: Power of Registrar to call for information
text: Registrar may require trade union officers to produce documents or financial accounts.

title: Participation Committee
text: (1) In every establishment employing 50 or more workers, employer shall constitute Participation Committee consisting of employer and worker representatives.

title: Functions of Participation Committee
text: Participation committee shall promote mutual trust, safety, health, occupational environment, and productivity.

title: Meetings of Participation Committee
text: Participation committee shall meet at least once every two months.

title: Implementation of Participation Committee recommendations
text:
Employer and trade union shall take steps to implement recommendations of Participation Committee.

CHAPTER XIII
SETTLEMENT OF INDUSTRIAL DISPUTE, LABOUR COURT, LABOUR APPELLATE TRIBUNAL, LEGAL PROCEEDINGS, ETC.

title: Raising of industrial dispute
text: An industrial dispute may be raised by Collective Bargaining Agent or employer in writing.

title: Conciliation
text: (1) Upon receipt of dispute notice, Conciliator appointed by Government shall start conciliation proceedings within ten days.

title: Settlement through conciliation
text: If agreement is reached in conciliation, memorandum of settlement shall be signed by parties and sent to Government.

title: Failure of conciliation
text: If conciliation fails within 30 days, Conciliator shall issue certificate of failure to parties.

title: Arbitration
text: Upon failure of conciliation, parties may agree to refer dispute to an Arbitrator chosen by them.

title: Strike and Lock-out
text: (1) CBA may issue 21 days' strike notice, or employer may issue 21 days' lock-out notice if conciliation fails and arbitration declined. (2) Three-fourths majority vote of CBA members required for strike call.

title: Prohibition of strike or lock-out in public utility services
text: Government may prohibit strike or lock-out in essential public utility services (power, water, gas, hospital, port).

title: Illegal strike or lock-out
text: A strike or lock-out commenced without proper notice, during conciliation/court proceedings, or in violation of Section 215 is illegal.

title: Establishment of Labour Courts
text: (1) The Government shall by notification establish one or more Labour Courts. (2) Labour Court consists of Chairman (Judicial Officer) and two members (one representing employers, one workers).

title: Jurisdiction of Labour Court
text: Labour Court shall adjudicate industrial disputes, wage claims, grievance petitions, trade union appeals, and offences under this Act.

title: Procedure and powers of Labour Court
text: Labour Court shall follow summary judicial procedure and have powers of Civil Court and Magistrate First Class.

title: Judgment and award of Labour Court
text: Labour Court shall deliver judgment within 60 days of application filing; award shall be binding on parties.

title: Appeal against Labour Court award
text: Party aggrieved by Labour Court award or sentence may appeal to Labour Appellate Tribunal within 45 days.

title: Labour Appellate Tribunal
text: (1) The Government shall establish Labour Appellate Tribunal consisting of Chairman (retired High Court Judge or Senior District Judge).

title: Procedure and powers of Labour Appellate Tribunal
text: Appellate Tribunal shall hear appeals from Labour Court and exercise superintendence over all Labour Courts.

title: Finality of Tribunal decisions
text: Judgment of Labour Appellate Tribunal shall be final and binding.

title: Settlement binding on all parties
text: Settlement reached in conciliation or award of Labour Court/Tribunal shall be binding on all workers and successor employers.

title: Period of operation of settlement or award
text: Settlement or award shall remain in force for period agreed or one year if no period specified.

title: Recovery of money due under award or settlement
text: Any money due from employer under settlement or award may be recovered as public demand or fine by Labour Court.

title: Appearance of legal practitioners
text: Parties before Labour Court or Tribunal may be represented by advocate or trade union officer.

title: Indemnity
text: No suit or legal proceeding shall lie against any public officer for anything done in good faith under this Act.

title: Costs of court proceedings
text: Costs of proceedings before Labour Court or Appellate Tribunal shall be at discretion of court.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text:
Government may issue orders to remove practical difficulties in implementing dispute settlements.

CHAPTER XIV
WORKERS' PARTICIPATION IN COMPANIES PROFITS

title: Application of Chapter XIV
text: This Chapter applies to every company/factory satisfying prescribed capital or asset threshold or employing 100 or more workers.

title: Establishment of Workers Participation Fund and Welfare Fund
text: Every company to which this Chapter applies shall establish a Workers' Participation Fund and a Workers' Welfare Fund.

title: Management of Funds
text: (1) Company shall pay 5% of its net profit every year to the Participation Fund, Welfare Fund, and Central Welfare Fund (80:10:10 ratio).

title: Board of Trustees
text: Management of Participation Fund and Welfare Fund shall vest in Board of Trustees consisting of company and worker representatives.

title: Allocation of Participation Fund
text: Two-thirds of Participation Fund shall be distributed equally among eligible workers in cash, and one-third invested.

title: Eligibility to participate in Fund
text: All workers with at least six months of continuous service in company shall be eligible to participate in Fund.

title: Exemption from tax
text: Contributions to and distributions from Participation Fund shall be exempt from income tax.

title: Audit of Fund accounts
text: Accounts of Participation Fund shall be audited annually by chartered accountant.

title: Recovery of unpaid contribution
text: Contribution unpaid by company to Fund may be recovered by Government as public demand with interest penalty.

title: Penalty for non-compliance
text: Failure by company officer to establish Fund or pay 5% profit share is punishable with fine up to Taka one lac and daily recurring fine.

title: Central Welfare Fund
text: Government shall manage Central Welfare Fund for benefit of industrial workers nationwide.

title: Power of Government to issue directions
text: Government may inspect Fund records and issue binding compliance directions to company.

title: Special provisions for export processing zones
text: Government may apply profit participation rules to EPZ and specialized economic zone units.

title: Annual report of Board of Trustees
text: Trustees shall submit annual report to Government showing profit share distribution.

title: Exemption of certain companies
text: Government may exempt specialized state enterprises or non-profit units from Chapter XIV.

title: Settlement of disputes regarding Fund
text: Disputes concerning eligibility or payout shall be decided by Labour Court.

title: Mode of investment of Fund
text: Unallocated fund amounts shall be invested in government securities or profitable bonds.

title: Prohibition of assignment or attachment
text: Worker's share in Fund shall not be attached by court order or assigned to third party.

title: Winding up of Participation Fund
text: Upon liquidation of company, Fund assets shall be distributed to eligible workers prior to general creditors.

title: Power to make rules under Chapter XIV
text: Government may make rules for calculation of net profit and trust administration.

title: Display of profit share statement
text:
Company shall display audited statement of profit share allocation within nine months of financial year end.

CHAPTER XV
PROVIDENT FUND

title: Establishment of Provident Fund in tea plantations
text: Every tea garden employer shall establish Provident Fund for resident workers.

title: Rate of contribution to Provident Fund
text: Worker contribution shall be 7.5% of basic wages, matched equally by 7.5% employer contribution.

title: Constitution of Board of Trustees for Provident Fund
text: Provident Fund shall be managed by Board of Trustees representing employer and workers equally.

title: Investment of Provident Fund money
text: Provident fund moneys shall be invested in approved government securities, treasury bills or fixed deposits.

title: Payment of Provident Fund on retirement or death
text: Accumulation in Provident Fund shall be paid to worker on retirement/resignation or to nominee on death.

title: Exemption from attachment
text: Amount standing to credit of worker in Provident Fund shall not be attached under court decree.

title: Provident fund in private establishments
text: Private establishments establishing voluntary provident fund shall register trust deed with Registrar.

title: Employers liability to pay provident fund
text: Employer failing to deposit monthly matching contribution shall be liable to pay penalty interest.

title: Recovery of provident fund dues
text: Unpaid provident fund dues may be recovered as public demand by Inspector or Trustee.

title: Protection of action taken in good faith
text: No suit shall lie against Trustee acting in good faith under Provident Fund rules.

title: Power to make rules regarding Provident Fund
text:
Government may make rules for provident fund accounts, audit, and withdrawal procedures.

CHAPTER XVI
ADMINISTRATION, INSPECTION, ETC.

title: Chief Inspector and Inspectors
text: Government shall appoint Chief Inspector, Additional Chief Inspectors, Deputy Chief Inspectors, and Inspectors of Factories and Establishments.

title: Powers of Chief Inspector
text: Chief Inspector shall exercise administrative supervision over all Inspectors and enforce compliance with this Act nationwide.

title: Powers of Inspectors
text: (1) Inspector may enter any establishment at any reasonable time, examine registers, take evidence, and inspect machinery and safety devices.

title: Inspectors to be public servants
text: Every Inspector appointed under this Act shall be deemed a public servant within meaning of Penal Code.

title: Employer to afford facilities to Inspector
text: Every employer shall afford all reasonable facilities to Inspector for entry, inspection, and examination.

title: Secrecy of information
text: Inspector shall keep confidential all manufacturing processes, trade secrets, and worker complaints coming to his knowledge.

title: Report of Inspector
text: Inspector shall submit periodic inspection reports to Chief Inspector detailing safety hazards and violations detected.

title: Power of Government to appoint experts
text: Government may appoint qualified medical, chemical, or engineering experts to assist Inspectors.

title: Delegation of powers
text: Chief Inspector may delegate any of his administrative powers to Deputy Chief Inspector or Inspector.

title: National Council for Industrial Health and Safety
text: Government shall establish National Council to advise on occupational safety and health policies.

title: Constitution of National Council
text: National Council shall consist of Minister of Labour, representatives of employers, workers, and health experts.

title: Functions of National Council
text: Council shall formulate national occupational safety guidelines, review accident trends, and recommend law amendments.

title: Maintenance of registers and records by employer
text: Employer shall maintain prescribed registers of workers, leave, wages, overtime, and accidents.

title: Display of notices
text: Employer shall display abstract of Act, working hours notice, and safety notices in Bangla and English at entrance.

title: Notice of local official address
text: Employer shall notify Inspector of official address and change of management within fifteen days.

title: Obligation of workers
text: No worker shall willfully interfere with safety appliance, commit unsafe act, or neglect health rules.

title: Right of worker to report unsafe condition
text: Worker may report dangerous machinery or unsafe condition to safety committee or Inspector.

title: Protection against victimization for reporting
text: No employer shall discipline worker for reporting safety violation or testifying before Inspector.

title: Annual report of Chief Inspector
text:
Chief Inspector shall submit annual national report to Government on administration of Act.

CHAPTER XVII
OFFENCES, PENALTIES AND PROCEDURE

title: Penalty for illegal strike or lock-out
text: Any worker who commences or continues illegal strike shall be punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Taka 5,000. Any employer commencing illegal lock-out punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Taka 25,000.

title: Penalty for instigating illegal strike or lock-out
text: Any person who instigates or incites others to take part in illegal strike/lock-out punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine.

title: Penalty for taking part in un-certificated union activities
text: Person taking part in illegal union activity or false CBA representation punishable with fine.

title: Penalty for unfair labor practices
text: Any person who commits unfair labor practice under Section 194 or 195 punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Taka 10,000.

title: Penalty for non-implementation of settlement or award
text: Failure to comply with settlement or Labour Court award punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine.

title: Penalty for paying less than minimum wages
text: Employer paying less than statutory minimum wage under Section 141 punishable with imprisonment up to 1 year or fine up to Taka 10,000.

title: Penalty for employment of child and adolescent
text: Employer employing child or adolescent in contravention of Chapter III punishable with fine up to Taka 5,000.

title: Penalty for failure to give notice of accident
text: Employer failing to report fatal accident or dangerous occurrence under Section 80 punishable with fine up to Taka 5,000.

title: Penalty for breach of safety rules
text: Breach of safety, health or fire precautions under Chapters V, VI, VII punishable with imprisonment up to 3 months or fine up to Taka 10,000.

title: Penalty for obstructing Inspector
text: Any person who willfully obstructs Inspector or hides documents punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine up to Taka 10,000.

title: Penalty for wrong statement or false register
text: Making false entry in service book, wage register or safety book punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine.

title: Penalty for failure to maintain participation committee
text: Employer failing to form Participation Committee under Section 205 punishable with fine.

title: Penalty for failure to pay profit share
text: Employer failing to pay 5% profit share into Workers' Participation Fund under Section 234 punishable with fine up to Taka 1,000,000.

title: Penalty for failure to provide creche or canteen
text: Employer failing to provide child room or canteen punishable with fine up to Taka 5,000.

title: Penalty for double employment of child
text: Parent or guardian permitting child to work in two establishments punishable with fine.

title: Offence by companies
text: Where offence under this Act is committed by company, every director, manager, secretary or officer shall be deemed guilty unless proved without knowledge.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court other than Labour Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under this Act.

title: Complaint by Inspector or aggrieved party
text: Labour Court shall take cognizance of offence only upon complaint in writing by Inspector, aggrieved worker, or trade union officer.

title: Limitation of prosecution
text: Prosecution for offence under this Act must be instituted within six months of date of offence knowledge.

title: Compounding of offences
text: Minor technical offences under this Act may be compounded by Chief Inspector upon payment of prescribed sum.

title: Trial procedure in Labour Court
text: Labour Court shall follow summary trial procedure prescribed in Code of Criminal Procedure for trial of offences.

title: Enhanced penalty after previous conviction
text: Person convicted of second offence under same provision shall be subject to double maximum fine or imprisonment.

title: Forfeiture of illegal wages or assets
text: Labour Court may order forfeiture of assets illegally gained through violation of Act.

title: Power to order repair of dangerous building
text: Labour Court may order employer to execute necessary structural repairs to dangerous building within specified time.

title: Penalty for breach of confidentiality
text: Inspector or officer breaching trade secret confidentiality punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months or fine.

title: Fine money utilization
text: Fines realized under this Act shall be credited to Government Treasury or Workers Welfare Foundation Fund.

title: Protection for acts done in good faith
text: No criminal prosecution shall lie against Government officer for act done in good faith under this Act.

title: Onus of proof regarding age
text: Where child age is disputed, onus of proving age lies on employer or parent producing medical certificate.

title: Onus of proof regarding safety compliance
text: In prosecution for failure to provide safety guard, onus of proving guard was provided lies on employer.

title: Execution of fine by Labour Court
text: Fines imposed by Labour Court may be recovered by distress and sale of offender's property.

title: Representation of accused
text: Accused employer or worker may defend himself through advocate or authorized representative.

title: Power of court to exempt employer in certain cases
text: Employer charged with offence may bring actual offender before court and be discharged if employer exercised due diligence.

title: Summary dismissal of frivolous complaints
text: Labour Court may dismiss frivolous or vexatious complaint and order complainant to pay compensation to accused.

title: Appeal against criminal conviction by Labour Court
text:
Appeal against conviction or sentence by Labour Court lies to Labour Appellate Tribunal within 30 days.

CHAPTER XVIII
MISCELLANEOUS

title: Power of Government to make rules
text: Government may by notification in official Gazette make rules for carrying out purposes of this Act.

title: Publication of rules
text: All rules made under Section 317 shall be subject to previous publication for public comments.

title: Power to exempt establishments
text: Government may by notification exempt any establishment, shop or factory from all or any provisions of this Act in public interest.

title: Display of abstracts of Act
text: Employer shall display abstract of Act and rules in clear Bangla script at prominent place in establishment.

title: Service of notice
text: Any notice, order or document required to be served under this Act may be served by registered post or hand delivery.

title: Protection of existing rights and privileges
text: Nothing in this Act shall affect any privilege, right or custom enjoyed by worker under any award, custom or agreement more favorable than this Act.

title: Freedom of contract subject to Act
text: Any contract of service whereby worker relinquishes any right conferred by this Act shall be void.

title: Bar of jurisdiction of Civil Courts
text: No Civil Court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which Labour Court or Tribunal is empowered to decide.

title: Members and staff of Labour Court to be public servants
text: Members, officers and staff of Labour Court and Tribunal shall be public servants.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to provisions of this Act, Government may by order make provisions not inconsistent with Act.

title: Protection of action taken under rules
text: No suit or legal proceeding shall lie against any person for anything done under rules made under this Act.

title: Power to amend Schedules
text: Government may by notification amend any Schedule to this Act (list of dangerous operations, diseases, compensation scale).

title: Training on Labour Law
text: Government and employers shall arrange periodic training on Labour Law and industrial safety for workers and managers.

title: Labour Statistics
text: Employer shall submit annual statistical returns regarding employment, wages, hours, and accidents to Chief Inspector.

title: Power to inspect records
text: Authorized government officers may call for and inspect employment records of any establishment.

title: Registration of establishments
text: Every establishment shall register with Department of Inspection for Factories and Establishments within prescribed time.

title: Renewal of establishment license
text: Factory and establishment licenses shall be renewed annually upon payment of prescribed fee.

title: Welfare Fund for Export Processing Zones
text: Specialized welfare fund rules shall apply to EPZ enterprises.

title: Application of Act to government establishments
text: Provisions of this Act apply to government industrial establishments and railway workshops.

title: Payment of dues of deceased worker
text: Unpaid wages and dues of deceased worker shall be paid to nominee or legal heir without probate certificate up to prescribed limit.

title: National Tripartite Consultative Council
text: Government shall constitute National Tripartite Consultative Council representing Government, employers, and workers to advise on labour policies.

title: Functions of Tripartite Council
text: Tripartite Council shall review labor laws, industrial harmony, productivity, and ILO convention compliance.

title: Gender equality in employment
text: Employer shall promote gender equality and non-discrimination in recruitment, training, and promotion.

title: Prevention of sexual harassment
text: Employer shall take effective measures and form complaint committee to prevent sexual harassment of women in workplace.

title: Equal opportunity for disabled workers
text: Employer shall encourage employment of physically challenged persons suitable for job.

title: Health center in large industrial zones
text: Government and employer associations may jointly establish medical centers in concentrated industrial areas.

title: Occupational health and safety policy
text: Every establishment employing 100 or more workers shall formulate written occupational safety and health policy.

title: Environmental protection in establishments
text: Establishment shall comply with environmental laws regarding industrial effluent and waste treatment.

title: Identity card for all workers
text: Employer shall issue identity card with photo to every worker at time of appointment free of charge.

title: Service book to be handed over on termination
text: Duplicate copy of service book shall be handed over to worker upon termination of employment.

title: Notice board requirement
text: Every establishment shall maintain notice board near main entrance for official notices.

title: Language of notices and agreements
text: All official notices, agreements and settlements shall be written in Bangla and English.

title: Translation of Act
text: Government shall publish authentic English translation of Bangladesh Labour Act 2006.

title: Computation of period of limitation
text: In computing period of limitation for filing application or appeal under this Act, provisions of Limitation Act apply.

title: Effect of law on custom or contract
text: Provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law or contract.

title: Overriding effect of Act
text: This Act shall override any inconsistent rule, regulation or instrument of establishment.

title: Repeal and savings
text: (1) The Factories Act 1965, Industrial Relations Ordinance 1969, Employment of Labour (Standing Orders) Act 1965, Payment of Wages Act 1936, Workmen's Compensation Act 1923, and Maternity Benefit Act 1939 are hereby repealed. (2) Anything done or action taken under repealed laws shall be deemed done under corresponding provision of this Act.

title: Original and authentic text
text: The original text of this Act is in Bangla, and the Government shall publish an authentic English text under Section 349.
